title: fig06 directed SPK-SPK Granger network built and run -- also null, third of three connectivity methods to fail the significance requirement
notes: New data product: scripts/extract_condition_spike_trials.py -- per-trial, per-area10 population-pooled spike-rate time series, RXRR/RRRR, matching fig05's LFP window/bins/conditions so the two networks share nodes and time base.

Real bug caught during the build: NWB filename suffix assumed uniform '_rec.nwb' across all sessions, silently dropping all 10 V182o sessions (which use plain '.nwb', no '_rec') on the first run -- 11/21 sessions, 92 keys. Found by directly listing D:/analysis/nwb rather than trusting the code, fixed to try both suffixes, re-run recovered all 21 sessions (166 keys).

jnwb.connectivity.directed_network() (method='granger', same settings as fig05: order='auto' BIC, max_lag=10, zscore-detrended) run per (session, condition) -- 42 calls across 21 sessions, 56s runtime (much faster than fig05's LFP version since there's no band dimension).

RESULT: also null. 0/45 tests survive Holm-Bonferroni across fig06_RXRR/fig06_RRRR/fig06_delta. Smallest raw p: MT<->TEO net directionality in BOTH RXRR (p=0.036, p_holm=0.32, n=8) and RRRR (p=0.050, p_holm=0.45, n=8) -- same pair, same direction, both conditions. Notable because MT<->TEO was ALSO fig05's smallest-p edge (low_gamma band, RRRR-vs-RXRR delta) -- a real cross-modality convergence worth a higher-powered follow-up, explicitly NOT reported as a finding since neither survives correction.

diagnostics_warning_rate=0.70 (lower than fig05's LFP Granger at 1.0, but still substantial) -- does not invalidate the group-level test (session-level point estimates are the unit of inference), but is a second reason not to over-read any single edge.

This is the THIRD connectivity method (of three attempted 2026-08-04) to fail the figures-4-7-require-significance rule: LFP-LFP coherency (0/240), LFP-LFP Granger (0/150), SPK-SPK Granger (0/45). Flagged to the user for a strategy decision rather than launching a fourth expensive method (TE) on this figure too without checking in -- TE is already running as a multi-hour background job for fig05.
issues: The recurring MT<->TEO signal across both fig05 (LFP low-gamma) and fig06 (spike Granger) is a real, if underpowered, cross-modality observation -- worth a dedicated, adequately-powered follow-up analysis if the manuscript ever wants to pursue it, but should not be cited as evidence in its current form (neither survives correction, n=8-9 sessions each).
plan: Awaiting user decision on strategy for fig05 (TE result pending) and fig06 (not yet attempted with TE, would face the same runtime tradeoff) before proceeding further.
